page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server operating on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz, the instance delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. This yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, delegating persistent disk operations entirely to network-attached block storage.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default. The 1:2 resource allocation makes this configuration cost-efficient for compute-heavy applications where memory consumption is low relative to active thread execution. Because memory is limited compared to typical general purpose ratios, applications requiring massive in-memory caching will encounter memory pressure.
This instance configuration is targeted at parallelized batch processing, frontend web serving clusters, continuous integration workers, light distributed compute nodes, and API proxy routing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 instance built on the KVM hypervisor, powered by an AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.25 GHz. It provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware profile includes no bundled local storage disks and no graphics processing units, relying on attached cloud storage volumes for file persistence. Network capabilities are defined by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps. With its lean memory footprint relative to its core count, the server offers efficient resource density for tasks that prioritize CPU concurrency over high RAM allocations. It is suitable for batch execution pipelines, microservice fleets, web serving layers, and CPU-driven build infrastructure.
